newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 21.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB) and IPB bank followed Komercni Banka yesterday and increased their interest rates. CSOB doubled its rate yesterday for all crown credits to 25 percent, and its reference rate increased to 24.6 percent. IPB's rates will increase tomorrow, its base rates will increase by five percent.
- The leader of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) and Chairman of Parliament Milos Zeman, should introduce his "package" of economic measures to his party members today.
- According to Transport Minister Martin Riman, railway reforms should save Czech Railways 4.2-5.0 billion crowns.
- The crown reacted to CSOB's increase in its base rate by climbing one percentage point to 1.7 percent below parity yesterday.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Civic Democratic Party (ODS) decided yesterday that during the next few days they will replace some of their eight cabinet members with new people in reaction to the continuing fall in trust in the cabinet and growing tension within the party.
- According to a survey from Factum, only every seventh Czech does not want changes in the cabinet.
- A survey from Factum shows that 23.9 percent of Czechs want Vaclav Klaus as Prime Minister, 17.1 percent want Josef Lux and 15.4 percent want Milos Zeman.
- Parliament supported another reading of a proposal for a law on bankruptcies, which should prevent bankruptcies of state or general hospitals.
- The opposition Social Democratic Party (CSSD) failed yesterday with its proposals for the state to regulate rents and to resolve relations between union organisations and employers.
- Today, the cabinet will decide between two possibilities from a proposal from the Labour and Social Affairs Ministry on how much pensions should rise.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After exactly 11 days, the general director of IPB bank and his deputy Libor Prochazka were released from jail. Apparently neither of them is hindering the course of the investigation, so it is unnecessary to hold them further.
- According to a survey from STEM, 71 percent of Czechs believe the state should control rents in private houses, seven years since the fall of socialism.
- The American ambassador to the Czech Republic expressed her opinion that the Czechs are discriminating against gypsies.
- Revenue for the government budget had increased on May 19 by 7.1 percent over the same time last year, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- The Agriculture Ministry approved aid for exports of beet sugar for 100 million crowns as part of a programme for the Export Support and Guarantee Farm and Forest Fund.

- The Industry and Trade Ministry yesterday presented delegates of the European Commission in Prague with a more detailed report explaining the reasons for introducing an import deposit for imports of food and consumer goods.

PRAVO - According to Jiri Nemec, the central director at Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna, increasing the value of points that doctors receive for examining patients to one crown from 65 hellers will cost the health care system 45 billion crowns yearly. He said that there is not enough money and the value will stay as it is.
- Skoda Mlada Boleslav will begin alternating production of Octavia cars between three factories between May and June.
- According to Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, the Finance Ministry already has material prepared for finishing privatisation of banks in an agreement with the Czech National Bank.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
